workflow_runs.name: CI
workflow_runs.display_title: fix(h2): replace a connection that stops responding after a stream timeout

head_commit.message:
fix(h2): replace a connection that stops responding after a stream timeout

A stream timeout only reset that stream, unlike HTTP/1.1 which destroys
the socket. When the connection itself silently died (dropped by a NAT or
load balancer, a hung peer), every new request was sent on it and timed
out in turn, and the Pool never opened a new connection.

On a stream timeout, send a PING and stop opening streams on the session
until it is acked. If no ack arrives within the timeout that fired, reset
the session so queued requests move to a fresh connection.

test(cache): use fake timers for the corrected-age tests

Real setTimeout in the origin handler made the response delay a wall-clock timer,
which is flaky under load. Switch to @sinonjs/fake-timers with toFake: ['Date'],

timer.

head_commit.message:
docs: clarify that `origin` is optional only for origin-bound dispatchers

Fixes #1011.

`Dispatcher.md` documented the `origin` option of `dispatcher.dispatch()` as
"(optional)", which reads as "never required". That only holds for a dispatcher
already bound to a single origin. `Agent` is not bound to one origin and
requires it.

Verified against current `main`:

  new Pool(origin).request({ path, method })   -> 200
  new Client(origin).request({ path, method })  -> 200
  new Agent().request({ path, method })         -> InvalidArgumentError
                                                'opts.origin must be a
                                                 non-empty string or URL.'
  new Agent().request({ origin, path, method }) -> 200

`Client`/`Pool` fill the origin from `this[kUrl].origin` when `kDispatch` builds
the Request (lib/dispatcher/client.js), while `Agent` rejects a missing origin
in its own `dispatch` (lib/dispatcher/agent.js). `docs/docs/api/Agent.md` already
calls `origin` "Required." for `Agent.dispatch()`; this aligns the abstract
Dispatcher docs with it.

Adds test/node-test/dispatcher-optional-origin.js to pin the distinction, which
had no test coverage.

Validation:
- node --test test/node-test/dispatcher-optional-origin.js   4/4 pass
- node --test test/node-test/agent.js                        35/35 pass
- node --test test/node-test/balanced-pool.js                25/25 pass
- eslint test/node-test/dispatcher-optional-origin.js         clean

Mutation checks, since a passing test is not the same as a protective test:
replacing `this[kUrl].origin` with `undefined` in the client's kDispatch
Request construction fails 3 of the 4 new tests, and dropping the origin
validation in Agent.dispatch fails 1 of 4.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(deduplicate): detach the primary on abort instead of rejecting the group

head_commit.message:
fix(deduplicate): detach the primary on abort instead of rejecting the group

Aborting the first request of a coalesced group cancelled the shared
dispatch, so every other caller waiting on it — including callers that
passed no signal — was rejected with an AbortError. Coalescing was not
transparent: whether your request succeeded depended on who asked first
and whether they had a timeout.

Hand the primary a proxied controller (same shape as the waiting
handlers). Aborting it now settles only the primary and detaches it from
the group; the underlying request is cancelled only once no member —
primary or waiting handler — is left waiting. This also releases the
pendingRequests entry when every member of a group aborts, so a later
request never joins a group with no consumers left. With no waiters the
abort still propagates exactly as before.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/5711
Signed-off-by: Paco Cartones <pacocartones@users.noreply.github.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams

head_commit.message:
fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams

When an HTTP/2 session is torn down with an error (e.g. the idle reaper
in onHttp2SessionIdleTimeout), Node fans that error out to every native
stream still tracked in the session's internal state. A released stream
that no longer has an 'error' listener then crashes the process with an
unhandled `InformationalError: socket idle timeout` (#5936).

releaseRequestStream, severRequestStream and releaseUpgradeStream only
installed a one-shot `once('error', noop)` sink (and not at all in
onError), so a single late error consumed it and the subsequent
session-level error went unhandled.

Keep a persistent `on('error', noop)` sink on every stream undici stops
tracking, and add a noop fallback in onError when the real handler is
removed. Retain the sink on upgrade streams instead of dropping it in
onUpgradeStreamClose.

Closes #5936.

fix(cache): always treat zero-lifetime entries as stale

Responses stored with a zero freshness lifetime (e.g. max-age=0 with an
etag) get staleAt === cachedAt. isStale() used `now > staleAt`, so a
reuse in the same millisecond as the store (or after the clock stepped
back) served the entry as fresh without revalidation. This made
'stores response with max-age=0 and etag, revalidates it on reuse'
flaky on CI.

head_commit.message:
fix(dns): share in-flight lookups between concurrent requests

Requests for the same hostname that arrive while a lookup is still in
flight now wait for that lookup instead of starting their own, so a cold
or expired cache no longer triggers a burst of identical lookups. Each
waiting request still picks its own address from the cached records. A
failed lookup rejects every waiting request and is not left pending, so
the next request retries it. Requests with per-request `dns` options keep
their own lookup.

Fixes #5974

head_commit.message:
feat(h2): add h2Options.maxConcurrentStreamsCap

maxConcurrentStreams is a fallback that the peer's SETTINGS frame
replaces, so a client cannot keep fewer streams per session than the
server allows. Add h2Options.maxConcurrentStreamsCap: when set, the
session limit is the lower of the server value and the cap. With a Pool
or Agent, a session at its cap counts as busy, so further requests open
another connection, up to `connections`.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/4143
Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/5134

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(eventsource): enforce maxEventSize on unterminated lines (#5814)

head_commit.message:
fix(eventsource): enforce maxEventSize on unterminated lines (#5814)

The eventSource.maxEventSize limit is only checked inside parseLine(),
which runs only when a line terminator (CR/LF) is reached. A server can
therefore stream a data: field (or any field) that never contains a line
terminator; the size check never runs and consumed chunks are never
reclaimed, so the client buffers the response body without bound, driving
the process toward memory exhaustion.

Track the in-progress line length (currentLineSize) and reject the stream
once it exceeds maxEventSize plus the longest data: field prefix. This
bounds any unterminated line against the configured cap while still
accepting a terminated data line whose value is exactly maxEventSize.

Adds regression tests for the unterminated-line bypass (stream and E2E)
and for the boundary case of a value equal to maxEventSize.
